# Gitdog - AI GitHub Assistant

> AI-powered assistant for GitHub repositories. Answers issues and discussions and reviews pull requests with codebase-aware evidence.

## About Gitdog

Gitdog is an AI automation platform for GitHub that helps developers automate repetitive tasks. When users mention @gitdogai in issues or discussions, the AI assistant analyzes the codebase context and provides intelligent, relevant responses. It also reviews pull requests and runs review commands from pull request comments and the gitdog CLI.

## Core Features

- **Issue Automation**: AI responds to issues with codebase-aware answers
- **Discussion Assistant**: Intelligent replies in GitHub Discussions
- **Pull Request Reviews**: Inline findings with source evidence, and approval when nothing is found
- **Context-Aware Answers**: Repository-specific guidance grounded in indexed code
- **Codebase Indexing**: Full repository understanding for accurate responses

## Commands

Gitdog reviews a pull request once, when it is opened or marked ready for review. When pull request reviews turn on, or a repository with them on is reactivated, reconnected or regains GitHub access, Gitdog also gives up to five open pull requests from the last 30 days their first review, skipping drafts and bots. After that, the pull request author or a repository collaborator asks for more:

| Pull request comment | CLI | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@gitdogai review` | `gitdog reviews request <ticket-id>` | Reviews the commits pushed since the last review |
| `@gitdogai full review` | `gitdog reviews request <ticket-id> --full` | Reviews the whole pull request again |
| `@gitdogai resolve` | `gitdog reviews resolve <ticket-id>` | Resolves every Gitdog review thread |
| `@gitdogai help` | `gitdog reviews --help` | Lists the commands |

A command is a comment line that starts with the mention, or follows another review bot's command on the same line. `@gitdogbot`, the app's former name, and the `@gitdog` shorthand also work. While a review runs, Gitdog keeps one status comment on the pull request up to date and removes it once the review is posted. Single reviews (not large pull requests reviewed in batches) also read the pull request conversation and list a reviewer's request the code does not make yet; a clean review approves only when no review thread from anyone is open, no reviewer has requested changes and nothing from the discussion is left open. Commands go in the pull request conversation; replies inside a review thread are not read, and pull requests opened by bots such as Dependabot are not reviewed. Collaborators can run every command; the pull request author, who may work from a fork, can run all but a full review. A review that failed or ran out of tokens can be requested again.

In issues and discussions, mention `@gitdogai` with a question to get a reply grounded in the repository.

- A review that finds no issues in fully reviewed changes approves the pull request; a later push, including updating the branch, withdraws the approval until `@gitdogai review` reviews the new commits.
- When a review cannot finish, for example because the account ran out of tokens, its status comment says why; for automatic reviews Gitdog posts at most one such comment a day per pull request.
- Someone who sends more than 10 commands an hour or 40 a day to one repository is paused there for 24 hours.

## Pricing

- **Free Plan**: $0/month - 100,000 one-time trial tokens, then your own Anthropic or OpenAI API key; prepaid token packs are available for additional usage
- **Pro Plan**: $9.99/month - 2.4M tokens/month; prepaid token packs are available for additional usage, with no automatic overage charges

## Technical Details

- Platform: Web application (SaaS)
- Integration: GitHub App
- Languages Supported: All programming languages
- Authentication: GitHub OAuth
